top_story: After Trump signaled on 23 July that a “massive attack” on Iran was imminent, the US on 24 July widened strikes across Iranian territory as Tehran retaliated with drones and attacks against American positions in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, while Washington also tied the escalation to Red Sea threats from the Houthis. By late 24 July, Trump was pairing expanded military pressure with claims of active US-Iran talks, suggesting Washington is trying to force negotiations from a position of escalation rather than de-escalation. In the occupied West Bank, a settler attack near Nablus that killed four Palestinians, alongside one settler and one Israeli officer, quickly fed revenge rhetoric and Israeli plans for an “extensive” operation, deepening the risk that regional war will intensify localized collective punishment. The immediate picture is a conflict system in which cross-border confrontation with Iran and internal Israeli-Palestinian violence are reinforcing each other, narrowing political space and raising civilian exposure across multiple fronts.
